conflict.intro: Sync found two versions of these notes and could not choose between them. Compare and decide what each note should hold — nothing is written until you confirm.

conflict.confirmMerge: Write the merged result into the note and permanently delete the conflict copy? Both original versions will be gone for good.

Every change and every presence message is encrypted on your device: the relay only learns which devices are connected to which note, when, and how large the messages are — never a single word of their content. Off by default, because it opens a permanent channel while a note is open. Notes in a shared vault do not depend on this setting: several people write to the same cloud object, so their room always opens — switching it off would not make them private, only silently conflicting.

byos.desc: Default is Filarr Cloud (R2). With Pro, Teams or Enterprise, your personal sync can live in your own S3 bucket — configurable here, on desktop and on the web.

byos.guideIntro: You stay a Filarr customer (account, email, devices). Only already-encrypted personal sync files can live in your S3 bucket.
byos.guideNotApi: You do not paste an API URL and you do not run a server. Link shares, Send and file requests stay on Filarr Cloud.
byos.guideWhere: Settings → Account & Sync → Where synced files live — in Filarr Desktop and on app.filarr.com alike. Your bytes never go through the browser: the Filarr server relays to your bucket.
byos.guidePlans: Pro, or a Teams / Enterprise org seat. Free and Solo see an upgrade prompt.
byos.guideStep1: Create a private bucket at the provider (R2, S3, Backblaze, Wasabi, Scaleway, OVH, MinIO…).
byos.guideStep2: Create an access key limited to that bucket, with read and write. Copy the secret once.
byos.guideStep3: In Filarr, click Use my bucket and pick the provider.
byos.guideStep4: Paste the HTTPS endpoint (origin only, no path), region, bucket name and both keys.
byos.guideStep5: R2 example: endpoint https://YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID.r2.cloudflarestorage.com — region auto — path-style addressing.
byos.guideStep6: S3 example: endpoint https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com — same region as the bucket — virtual-hosted addressing.
byos.guideStep7: Click Test (HeadBucket, 5 s). If reachable, Save. The next sync sends blobs to your bucket.
byos.guideStep8: After saving, the “Bring your data over” panel copies whatever still sleeps on Filarr Cloud — server-to-server, stoppable and resumable.
byos.guideLimits: Two target changes per 7 days (one if the endpoint is “Other”). Switching back to Filarr Cloud does not empty your bucket at the provider.
byos.guideLapse: If the subscription ends: no more writes, reads for ~30 days, then Filarr stops talking to the bucket. Files stay at the provider.
byos.guideFailUnreachable: Wrong endpoint (not the marketing website URL), wrong region, or keys that cannot ListBucket / HeadBucket.
byos.guideFailEndpoint: Public HTTPS only: no http://, no localhost, no private IP, no path in the URL.
byos.guideFailPlan: Pro (or a Teams seat) is enforced on the server, not only in the UI.

byos.healthHint: Filarr probes your bucket every few hours and emails you after three consecutive failures. Sync stops while it is unreachable — it never assumes the cloud is empty.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.content:
Welcome to **Filarr Notes** — your personal knowledge management system built right into Filarr.

**Create your first note:** Click the **+** button in the Notes sidebar, or press `Ctrl+N`.

**Write freely:** The editor supports rich text, markdown shortcuts, slash commands, and more. Just start typing.

**Connect your knowledge:** Type `[[` to create wiki-links between notes, files, and folders. These connections build your personal knowledge graph.

**Daily journaling:** Press `Ctrl+Shift+D` to create (or open) today's daily note — perfect for journaling, stand-ups, or daily logs.

**Explore views:** Switch between List, Masonry, Kanban, Sticky Notes, Database, Tasks, Calendar, Mind Map and Graph views using the view toggle bar at the top.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
shortcuts.content:
**Navigation:**
- `Ctrl+N` — Create a new note
- `Ctrl+Shift+D` — Open/create today's daily note
- `Ctrl+Shift+G` — Toggle graph view
- `Ctrl+P` — Open command palette

**Text Formatting:**
- `Ctrl+B` — Bold
- `Ctrl+I` — Italic
- `Ctrl+U` — Underline
- `Ctrl+Shift+X` — Strikethrough
- `Ctrl+Shift+H` — Highlight text

**Editor Shortcuts:**
- `/` — Open slash command menu
- `[[` — Insert wiki-link with autocomplete
- `#` at start of line — Heading (## for H2, ### for H3)
- `-` or `*` at start — Bullet list
- `1.` at start — Numbered list
- `[]` at start — Task/checkbox
- `>` at start — Blockquote
- `---` — Horizontal rule
- ` ``` ` — Code block

interfaceOverview.title: Interface Overview
interfaceOverview.content:
The Notes interface is divided into three main areas:

**Left Panel — Notes List:**
- Browse, search, sort, and filter your notes
- Create new notes, daily notes, or notes from templates
- Pin important notes to keep them at the top
- Access Flashcards, Templates, and this Wiki

**Center — Editor:**
- Rich text editor powered by TipTap
- Floating bubble menu for quick formatting (select text to see it)
- Toolbar at top with formatting, version history, and export
- Breadcrumb trail showing recently visited notes
- Slash commands (`/`) for inserting blocks

**Right Panel — Backlinks & Smart Tags:**
- See which notes link to the current one (backlinks)
- Discover potential unlinked mentions
- View outgoing links
- Get AI-suggested tags based on content analysis

bubbleMenu.title: Floating Bubble Menu
bubbleMenu.content:
When you **select text** in the editor, a floating toolbar appears with quick formatting options:

- **Bold**, **Italic**, **Underline**, **Strikethrough**
- **Code** (inline monospace)
- **Highlight** with color picker (8 colors available)
- **Link** insertion

The bubble menu follows your selection and disappears when you click away. It's the fastest way to format text without leaving the keyboard.

slashCommands.title: Slash Commands
slashCommands.content:
Type `/` at the beginning of a new line to open the **slash command menu**. Available commands:

**Text blocks:**
- `/heading1`, `/heading2`, `/heading3` — Section headings
- `/paragraph` — Normal text

**Lists:**
- `/bulletlist` — Unordered list
- `/orderedlist` — Numbered list
- `/tasklist` — Checkboxes / to-do list

**Content:**
- `/blockquote` — Quote block
- `/codeblock` — Code with syntax highlighting
- `/table` — Insert a table
- `/horizontalrule` — Divider line
- `/image` — Embed an image
- `/file` — Embed a file from your library

Start typing after `/` to filter commands. Press Enter or click to insert.

highlightColors.title: Highlight Colors
highlightColors.content:
Filarr Notes supports **multicolor highlighting** — perfect for color-coding different types of information.

**How to use:**
- Select text and click the highlight button in the bubble menu or toolbar
- Choose from 8 preset colors: yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red, orange, gray
- Click the same color again to remove the highlight

**Use cases:**
- **Yellow** for key takeaways
- **Green** for action items
- **Blue** for references and sources
- **Red** for warnings or critical items
- **Purple** for ideas and brainstorming

dragDropBlocks.title: Drag & Drop Blocks
dragDropBlocks.content:
Rearrange content blocks by dragging them:

**How it works:**
- Hover over any block (paragraph, heading, list, etc.) — a **drag handle** (6 dots) appears on the left
- Click and hold the handle to start dragging
- Drop the block at a new position — a blue insertion line shows where it will land

**Supported blocks:**
- Paragraphs, headings, blockquotes
- Lists (entire list or individual items)
- Code blocks, tables
- Embedded files and images

This makes it easy to reorganize your notes without cutting and pasting.

editorThemes.title: Editor Themes
editorThemes.content:
Customize the editor's look and feel with three built-in themes:

**Default** — Clean, balanced design with the standard Filarr look.

**Writer** — Optimized for long-form writing:
- Serif font (Georgia) for comfortable reading
- Warm cream-tinted background
- Wider line spacing
- Centered, narrower text column

**Developer** — Designed for technical notes:
- Monospace font (JetBrains Mono / Fira Code)
- Dark-friendly styling
- Better code block contrast

**Switch themes:** Use the theme selector dropdown in the editor toolbar. Your choice persists across sessions.

wikiLinks.title: Wiki-Links
wikiLinks.content:
**Wiki-links** are the core of the knowledge graph. They connect your notes bidirectionally.

**Create a link:** Type `[[` and start typing a name. The autocomplete shows:
- **Notes** — your existing notes
- **Files** — documents in your library (use `[[file:document.pdf]]`)
- **Folders** — your folder structure (use `[[folder:Projects]]`)

**How links work:**
- Clicking a wiki-link opens the linked note
- `Ctrl+Click` opens the linked note in a split panel
- Links are bidirectional — if Note A links to Note B, Note B shows a backlink to Note A

**Link syntax:**
- `[[Note Title]]` — Link to a note
- `[[file:filename.pdf]]` — Link to a file
- `[[folder:FolderName]]` — Link to a folder
- `![[Note Title]]` — Embed (transclude) a note inline

backlinks.title: Backlinks & Auto-Links
backlinks.content:
The **Backlinks Panel** (right side of the editor) shows all connections to the current note:

**Backlinks** — Notes that explicitly link to this note via `[[wiki-links]]`. Shows a context snippet around each mention.

**Outgoing Links** — Notes, files, and folders that this note links to.

**Potential Links** (Auto-detected) — Other notes that mention this note's title in their text but haven't created an explicit link yet. Click the "+" to convert a mention into a link.

**Orphan Detection** — Notes with no incoming or outgoing links are flagged with an orange "unlinked" badge in the notes list, helping you discover disconnected knowledge.

transclusion.title: Transclusion (Note Embedding)
transclusion.content:
**Transclusion** lets you embed the content of one note inside another.

**Syntax:** Use `![[Note Title]]` (note the exclamation mark before the brackets).

**What happens:**
- The referenced note's content appears inline as a bordered, read-only card
- The embedded content updates live — edit the source note and the transclusion refreshes
- Click the transclusion to navigate to the source note

**Use cases:**
- Create a "dashboard" note that aggregates sections from multiple notes
- Reuse definitions, templates, or reference material across notes
- Build a master document from modular components

breadcrumb.title: Breadcrumb Navigation
breadcrumb.content:
The **breadcrumb trail** appears above the editor, showing the last notes you visited.

- Up to **10 recent notes** are tracked
- Click any breadcrumb to jump back to that note
- The trail resets to the current note when you navigate
- Useful for quickly switching between related notes you're working on

The breadcrumb is your "back" button for note navigation — no need to search for notes you just had open.

hoverPreview.title: Link Preview on Hover
hoverPreview.content:
Hover over any `[[wiki-link]]` in the editor to see a **preview popover** without leaving the current note.

The preview shows:
- Note title
- First ~150 characters of the note content
- Word count and link count
- Last updated date

This lets you quickly check what a linked note contains before deciding to navigate to it.

splitEditing.title: Split Note Editing
splitEditing.content:
Open two notes side by side:

**How:** Hold `Ctrl` and click a wiki-link. The linked note opens in a new panel to the right.

This uses Filarr's tab system — you can have multiple notes open in separate tabs and split panels.

**Use cases:**
- Compare two notes
- Reference material while writing
- Copy content between notes
- Review linked notes without losing your place

listView.title: List View
listView.content:
The default view — a traditional **sidebar + editor** layout.

**Left sidebar shows:**
- All notes sorted by date, title, or word count
- Search bar to filter notes instantly
- Sort controls (Modified, Title, Created, Words) with ascending/descending toggle
- Note count
- Pinned notes appear at the top

**Right side:** The full editor with toolbar, bubble menu, and backlinks panel.

**Tip:** Pin frequently accessed notes to keep them at the top of the list regardless of sort order.

masonryView.title: Masonry View
masonryView.content:
**Pinterest-style card grid** showing all your notes as cards.

Each card displays:
- Note title
- First ~100 characters of content preview
- Word count and link count
- Cover color (if set)
- Daily note badge

Cards are arranged in a responsive masonry layout that fills available space. Click any card to open it in the editor.

**Best for:** Visual overview of all notes, quickly scanning content, finding notes by appearance.

kanbanView.title: Kanban View
kanbanView.content:
Organize notes into **columns** — perfect for project management and workflows.

**Default columns:** Inbox, In Progress, Review, Done.

**Features:**
- **Drag & drop** notes between columns to change their status
- **Add columns** — click "+" to create custom columns
- **Delete columns** — hover a column header and click the trash icon
- Notes are automatically saved to their column

**How it works internally:** The column assignment is stored in the note's metadata, so moving between columns is instant.

**Best for:** Project tracking, content pipelines, task management, sprint planning.

stickyNotesView.title: Sticky Notes View
stickyNotesView.content:
A **free-form 2D canvas** where notes appear as colored sticky notes.

**Controls:**
- **Drag** a sticky note to reposition it
- **Scroll wheel** to zoom in/out
- **Shift+click** and drag on the background to pan the canvas
- Notes snap to a 20px grid for clean alignment

**Colors:** Each note gets a color from the palette (yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, orange). Colors cycle automatically.

**Best for:** Brainstorming, mind mapping, spatial organization, visual thinkers.

graphView.title: Graph View
graphView.content:
The **Graph View** visualizes your knowledge as an interactive network.

**Node types:**
- **Circles** (blue) = Notes
- **Squares** (green) = Files
- **Hexagons** (yellow) = Folders

**Node size** reflects how many connections each item has.

**Interactions:**
- **Click** a node to select and open it
- **Drag** nodes to rearrange the layout
- **Scroll** to zoom in/out
- **Click + drag** on empty space to pan

**Edge types:**
- Solid lines = note-to-note links
- Dashed lines = note-to-file or note-to-folder links

The graph uses a real-time **force-directed layout** — nodes repel each other and edges pull connected nodes together.

graphClusters.title: Automatic Clusters
graphClusters.content:
Enable **Clusters** to automatically group densely connected notes.

**How it works:**
- Uses a simplified **Louvain algorithm** for community detection
- Notes that are heavily interconnected form a cluster
- Each cluster gets a unique color
- A legend shows all clusters with their colors

**Toggle:** Click the cluster icon in the graph toolbar (top-left, three-circle icon).

**Insights:** Clusters reveal hidden structure in your knowledge — topics you've written about extensively tend to form tight groups. Isolated clusters might indicate disconnected areas worth bridging.

graphHeatmap.title: Heat Map Mode
graphHeatmap.content:
Toggle the **heat map** to visualize note recency.

**Color coding:**
- **Red/Hot** — Recently edited notes (today/yesterday)
- **Yellow/Warm** — Edited this week
- **Blue/Cold** — Older, stale notes

**Toggle:** Click the flame/pin icon in the graph toolbar.

**Insights:** The heat map reveals which parts of your knowledge base are actively maintained and which areas might need revisiting. Cold clusters are opportunities for review.

Note: Clusters and Heat Map are mutually exclusive — enabling one disables the other.

graphFilter.title: Graph Filter
graphFilter.content:
Use the **search bar** in the graph toolbar to filter nodes by title.

**How it works:**
- Type a search term in the filter input
- Matching nodes remain fully visible
- Non-matching nodes fade to 12% opacity (they're still there, just dimmed)
- Edges to dimmed nodes also fade

**Use cases:**
- Focus on a specific topic area
- Find where a particular note sits in your knowledge graph
- Explore the neighborhood of a specific node

graphTimeTravel.title: Time Travel
graphTimeTravel.content:
The **Time Travel** slider lets you see your knowledge graph as it was at any point in time.

**How to use:**
- Click the clock icon in the graph toolbar to enable time travel
- A slider appears below the toolbar
- Drag the slider to scrub through time
- Notes created after the selected date are hidden
- The current date is displayed next to the slider

**Use cases:**
- See how your knowledge base has grown over time
- Review what you knew at a specific point
- Identify when connections were formed

templates.title: Templates
templates.content:
**Templates** provide pre-structured content for common note types.

**Built-in templates:**
- **Meeting Notes** — Attendees, agenda, decisions, action items
- **Decision Log** — Context, options considered, decision, rationale
- **Weekly Review** — Accomplishments, challenges, next week's goals
- **Brainstorm** — Topic, ideas, evaluation, next steps

**Using a template:** Open the Template Manager (grid icon in the sidebar), browse templates, and click "Use Template".

**Custom templates:** Open any note, then click "Save as Template" at the bottom of the sidebar. Your note's content becomes a reusable template.

**Variables:** Templates support `{{date}}`, `{{title}}`, and other placeholders that are automatically filled when you create a note from the template.

dailyNotes.title: Daily Notes
dailyNotes.content:
**Daily notes** are automatically dated journal entries — one per day.

**Create:** Press `Ctrl+Shift+D` or click the calendar icon in the sidebar.

**Naming:** Daily notes use the format "YYYY-MM-DD" (e.g., "2026-03-14").

**Smart carry-over:** When you create a new daily note, any **unchecked tasks** from the previous day's note are automatically carried over to the new note under a "Carried Over" heading. This ensures nothing falls through the cracks.

**Badge:** Daily notes have a calendar icon badge in the notes list to distinguish them from regular notes.

**Best for:** Daily journals, stand-up notes, work logs, habit tracking.

pinning.title: Pinning Notes
pinning.content:
**Pin** important notes to keep them at the top of the sidebar, regardless of sort order.

**How:** Click the pin icon on any note card, or right-click and select "Pin".

Pinned notes have a subtle pin badge and are always visible at the top of the list. This is useful for:
- Quick access to frequently referenced notes
- Keeping project dashboards visible
- Marking notes you're actively working on

sortingSearching.title: Sorting & Searching
sortingSearching.content:
**Search:** The search bar at the top of the sidebar filters notes instantly as you type. It searches both titles and content.

**Sort options** (click the sort icon to cycle):
- **Modified** — Most recently edited first (default)
- **Title** — Alphabetical order
- **Created** — Newest notes first
- **Words** — Longest notes first

**Sort order:** Click the arrow (up/down) to toggle ascending/descending.

**Note count:** The total number of matching notes is shown next to the sort controls.

smartTags.title: Smart Tags (AI Suggestions)
smartTags.content:
Filarr uses **TF-IDF analysis** to automatically suggest relevant tags for your notes.

**How it works:**
- The algorithm analyzes the text of all your notes
- It finds keywords that are **distinctive** to each note (common words across all notes are de-prioritized)
- The top 5 keyword suggestions appear below the Backlinks panel
- Supports both **English and French** stop word filtering

**Adding a tag:** Click the "+" button next to any suggestion to create and apply the tag to your note.

**TF-IDF explained:** Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency is a statistical measure that evaluates how important a word is to a document in a collection. Words that appear frequently in one note but rarely in others get higher scores.

orphanDetection.title: Orphan Detection
orphanDetection.content:
**Orphan notes** are notes with no incoming or outgoing wiki-links — they're disconnected from your knowledge graph.

**Identification:** Orphan notes display an orange dot badge in the notes list.

**Why it matters:** Orphaned notes represent knowledge that isn't connected to anything else. You might want to:
- Add wiki-links to connect them to related notes
- Check if they contain useful information worth linking
- Delete them if they're no longer needed

**Backlinks Panel:** When viewing an orphan note, the backlinks panel shows "No connections" and suggests creating links.

folderNotes.title: Notes in Folders
folderNotes.content:
Notes can be **associated with folders** in your file system, appearing alongside your files.

When notes are linked to a folder, they show up as compact cards in the Folder View, below the files section.

**Click** a note card in the folder view to open it in the Notes editor.

This bridges the gap between your document library and your knowledge system — meeting notes can live next to meeting files, project notes next to project documents.

versioning.title: Version History
versioning.content:
Filarr automatically saves **version snapshots** of your notes as you edit.

**How it works:**
- Snapshots are taken every **30 seconds** (minimum interval between versions)
- Up to **20 versions** are kept per note (oldest are pruned)
- Each version stores the full content, title, and word count

**Viewing history:** Click the **clock icon** in the editor toolbar to open the Version History panel.

**Features:**
- **Timeline** — Browse all saved versions with timestamps
- **Diff view** — Click "Show Diff" to see what changed between two versions (green = added, red = removed)
- **Restore** — Click "Restore" on any version to revert the note to that state

**Storage:** Versions are stored locally in your profile storage — they persist across sessions.

export.title: Multi-Format Export
export.content:
Export your notes in five formats:

**Markdown (.md)** — Clean plain text with formatting. Perfect for sharing, publishing, or migrating to other tools.

**HTML (.html)** — Fully styled web page. Includes Filarr's typography and can be opened in any browser.

**PDF (.pdf)** — Portable document. Good for printing or sharing formal documents.

**DOCX (.docx)** — Microsoft Word format. Ideal for collaboration with people who use Word.

**Filarr (.filarr)** — Complete backup including all metadata, wiki-links, tags, and version history. Use this for full backups or transferring between Filarr installations.

**How to export:** Click the **download icon** in the editor toolbar to open the Export dialog. Choose your format, toggle options (include metadata, include links), and click Export.

flashcards.title: Flashcards
flashcards.content:
Create **flashcards** from your notes for spaced repetition learning.

**Adding Q&A pairs:** Write questions and answers in your notes using these formats:

`Q: What is a wiki-link?`
`A: A bidirectional link between notes using [[brackets]]`

Or the shorter format:
`? Question here`
`! Answer here`

**Generating a deck:** Open the Flashcard view (card icon in the sidebar header), then click "Generate from Notes" to scan all your notes for Q&A pairs.

**Reviewing:**
- Cards show the question first
- Click "Reveal" to see the answer
- Rate your recall: Again, Hard, Good, or Easy
- The **SM-2 algorithm** schedules cards for optimal review intervals

**Spaced repetition:** Cards you find easy are shown less frequently. Cards you struggle with are shown more often. This scientifically optimizes your learning.

fileEmbed.title: File & Image Embedding
fileEmbed.content:
Embed files and images directly in your notes.

**Methods:**
- Use the slash command `/image` or `/file`
- Drag and drop a file from the Filarr file explorer into the editor

**Supported previews:**
- **Images** (PNG, JPG, GIF, SVG) — inline image preview
- **Videos** (MP4, WebM) — video player
- **Documents** (PDF, DOCX, etc.) — file card with icon and name

**File cards** show the file name, type icon, and size. Click a file card to open it in Filarr's file viewer.

This lets you create rich notes that combine text with visual and document references.

markdownShortcuts.title: Markdown Shortcuts
markdownShortcuts.content:
The editor recognizes common **Markdown syntax** and converts it to rich text automatically:

- `# Heading 1`, `## Heading 2`, `### Heading 3`
- `**bold**` → **bold**
- `*italic*` → *italic*
- `~~strikethrough~~` → ~~strikethrough~~
- `==highlight==` → highlighted text
- `\`code\`` → inline code
- `- item` or `* item` → bullet list
- `1. item` → numbered list
- `[] task` → task checkbox
- `> quote` → blockquote
- `---` → horizontal rule
- `\`\`\`` → code block

These shortcuts work inline as you type — no need to switch modes. The text is converted to rich content immediately.

fullTextSearch.title: Full-Text Search
fullTextSearch.content:
Filarr Notes uses **FlexSearch** for instant full-text search across all your notes.

**Features:**
- Search by content, title, or both
- Results appear as you type with highlighted snippets
- Prefix queries: type `title:keyword` to search only in titles
- Handles thousands of notes with sub-millisecond response times

**Where it's used:**
- The search bar in the Notes sidebar
- Wiki-link autocomplete (`[[`)
- Command palette

**Technical details:** The search index is built in-memory from your Redux store and updates automatically as you create, edit, or delete notes. It uses tokenized indexing for fast fuzzy matching.

tips.title: Tips & Best Practices
tips.content:
**Build connections gradually.** Don't worry about creating the perfect structure upfront. Add wiki-links as you write, and the graph will emerge naturally.

**Use daily notes as an inbox.** Capture thoughts in your daily note, then refine and link them to permanent notes later.

**Review orphans regularly.** Check the orphan badges in your notes list — these are notes that could benefit from connections.

**Use templates for recurring notes.** Meeting notes, weekly reviews, and project logs are perfect candidates for templates.

**Leverage the graph.** Switch to Graph View periodically to discover unexpected connections and identify knowledge gaps.

**Export for backup.** Use the Filarr (.filarr) export format periodically for a complete backup of your knowledge base with all metadata intact.

**Keyboard-first workflow.** Learn `Ctrl+N`, `Ctrl+Shift+D`, `/`, and `[[` — these four shortcuts cover 90% of note creation and linking.

freeze.title: Freeze the vault
freeze.hint: Close a finished project without destroying it: the vault stays readable, but nobody writes to it any more.
freeze.confirm: What freezing stops: every change to the CONTENT — uploading, editing, renaming, moving, deleting, restoring from the trash, and sealing a new per-item access. Nothing is destroyed and nobody loses access: everyone keeps reading and downloading. What it does NOT stop: removing someone, revoking an invitation, renewing the key, changing settings, leaving the vault, and unfreezing. Any admin can unfreeze it at any moment.

governance.title: Governance & offline enforcement
governance.desc: How your governance policies actually apply across member devices — and what is, and is not, enforceable.
governance.bestEffort: Policy enforcement is best-effort and client-applied. A device that is offline keeps running the policy it last cached, so a hardened policy is not instantly universal. The Worker remains authoritative for what it can enforce server-side: token issuance/refresh, IP allowlist, and remote sign-out at next connect.
governance.pending: Pending (offline devices on a cached policy)
governance.offlineCaveat: Offline devices apply the cached idle-lock and grace window locally (forgetting their key after {{days}} days offline), but absolute-session expiry, IP allowlist, policy updates, and remote-wipe only take effect at the next successful connection. These local guards are best-effort and can be bypassed offline by a determined user who holds the password.

offline.banner: Offline — enforcing the org policy cached on {{date}}. Some controls (network allowlist, remote sign-out) only apply online; client guards are best-effort.

degraded.lock: Your organization requires a policy re-sync. This device has been offline past the allowed grace window, so the vault was locked. Reconnect to restore full access — offline unlock remains best-effort.

retention.title: Data retention (client-applied)
retention.caveat: Retention runs on each member device: version history is pruned as notes are saved, and trashed items are purged on a periodic sweep. It is best-effort (a determined offline user can defer it). IMPORTANT: it does NOT yet exclude a member's LOCAL data under a legal hold — a held member's trashed notes and old versions may still be pruned on their own device. The authoritative synced/vault copy stays preserved by the server-side legal-hold gates; full client-side hold exclusion is planned.

dlp.title: Data loss prevention (DLP)
dlp.body: Filarr is zero-knowledge: the server only ever holds ciphertext, so it cannot scan or classify your content — there is no server-side content DLP, and we never claim there is. Your real DLP controls are the metadata/ciphertext ones above: share governance, session/IP allowlist, device revoke + remote-wipe, retention + legal hold, and the tamper-evident audit log. To plug into an endpoint-DLP or SIEM (CrowdStrike, Microsoft Purview, Splunk…), add an audit Sink (the SIEM tab) pointing at your collector — Filarr streams metadata-only events (never content) for it to act on. Post-decryption controls (no-copy/print/watermark) cannot be server-enforced and are only ever a best-effort endpoint agent.

policy.title: Governance policy
policy.desc: Org-wide security controls, enforced server-side. Metadata only — never your vault keys.

mfaRequired.label: Require two-factor authentication
mfaRequired.desc: Members must enrol 2FA to complete a password login. SSO members: configure MFA at your identity provider.

reauth.label: Re-authenticate for sensitive actions
reauth.desc: Prompt for a fresh login before escrow, policy or billing changes.

idleTimeout.label: Idle timeout (minutes)
idleTimeout.desc: Auto-lock after this many idle minutes. Empty = no limit.

absoluteTimeout.label: Absolute session limit (minutes)
absoluteTimeout.desc: Force re-login after this long regardless of activity. Empty = no limit.

offlineGrace.label: Offline grace (days)
offlineGrace.desc: Days a device may run offline on its cached policy before it locks. Empty = client default (30).

externalShares.label: Block external share links
externalShares.desc: Prevent members from creating public/external shares and Filarr Send links.

restrictDownload.label: View-only (block download of shared content)
restrictDownload.desc: Removes download gestures for read-only roles, in the app. Client-enforced, best-effort: end-to-end encryption means a viewer holds the key — no interface can truly prevent them from reconstructing a file.

maxExpiry.label: Maximum share expiry (days)
maxExpiry.desc: Cap how long a share can live. Empty = uncapped.

retention.heading: Retention
retention.note: Retention is applied on each member device (the encrypted data lives there, not on the server).

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.desc: What the app offers the members of your organization: marketplace, extensions, appearance.
workspace.honesty: Settings marked "enforced by the server" are applied by Filarr whatever state the device is in: the catalogue, extension installs and publishing all go through our servers, and a refusal there is final. Settings marked "best-effort" are applied by the app itself — a determined user on a modified device can work around them. We would rather tell you than let you believe in a protection we do not hold.
workspace.marketplaceDisabledDesc: No extensions, no layout templates. The sidebar entry disappears and the server refuses the catalogue.
workspace.layoutMarketDisabledDesc: Layout templates only — extensions stay available.
workspace.publishingDisabledDesc: Your members can install, but not publish an extension or template under their account.

mode.openDesc: Everyone installs what they want from the catalogue.
mode.allowlistDesc: Only the extensions you name can be installed and loaded.
mode.blockedDesc: No third-party extensions. Already-installed ones stop loading.

workspace.defaultThemeDesc: Applied on your members' devices. Without a lock, each of them stays free to change it.
workspace.themeLockedDesc: The theme picker disappears from your members' settings, naming your organization.
workspace.defaultFontDesc: Same idea as the theme: a default, or an enforced choice.
workspace.fontLockedDesc: The font picker disappears from your members' settings.

guide.title: Guide
guide.adminDesc: The order of setup, and what each step commits you to. Steps tick themselves from your organization's real state.
guide.memberDesc: What joining an organization changes for you, and what your organization can — and cannot — see.
guide.notAdmin: You are reading an administrator's path. Your role does not let you perform these steps, but knowing what was set up for you is part of it.
guide.remaining: {{n}} step(s) left before your organization is operational.

name.title: Name your organization
name.body: The name appears to your members, in the invitations you send and on your branded deposit pages. You can change it at any time.

escrow.title: Create your organization key
escrow.body: It is what will let you give access back to a member who lost their password. It gives us no access to your content: we hold only encrypted copies, useless without yours.
escrow.warning: Do this BEFORE inviting your members. Recovery only covers vaults sealed after the key is in place: a vault created before it stays unrecoverable if its owner loses their password.

invite.title: Invite your team
invite.body: Every invitation carries a role. Viewers do not count towards your bill: invite as many as you need. Other roles take a seat, with a minimum of three.

roles.title: Understand the roles
roles.body: Owner: everything, including deleting the organization and transferring ownership. Admin: members, roles, billing, settings. Security admin: audit log and SIEM streaming, with no power over members or billing. Editor and viewer: no administration at all, only access to the vaults shared with them.
roles.warning: No role, not even yours, can read a member's files. Administration governs access, never decryption: that depends on keys which never leave the devices.

policies.title: Set your policies
policies.body: Session length, allowed IP ranges, mandatory two-factor authentication, sharing rules, retention. Each setting states whether our servers enforce it or the app applies it best-effort.

workspace.title: Set up the workspace
workspace.body: Turn off the marketplace, allow only certain extensions, apply — or enforce — a theme and a font. Since the catalogue and installs go through our servers, a refusal there is final.

audit.title: Know what the log holds
audit.body: Sign-ins, role changes, shares created or revoked, admin actions. Metadata only: never a file’s content nor a note’s title. The log is chained — a removed or altered line shows — and exports to CSV.

subscribe.title: Subscribe
subscribe.body: Until the subscription is taken out, your organization exists but grants nothing: no invitations, no team vaults, no branding. This is the first thing to do. Billing is per seat, with a minimum of three, and viewers do not count.
subscribe.bodyDone: Your organization has the full plan: team vaults, file requests, branding, audit log, policies and org-key recovery.
subscribe.warning: Cancel any time. When the subscription stops, the plan pauses: your data stays intact and becomes read-only. Nothing is deleted, and re-subscribing restores writing immediately.

joined.title: You joined {{org}}
joined.body: Your organization account is separate from any personal Filarr account: what you put here belongs to work, what you put there does not and is not visible from this organization.

privacy.title: What your organization sees — and does not
privacy.body: It sees administrative metadata: your email address, your role, your sign-ins, the shares you create, the devices you enrol. It DOES NOT SEE the content of your files or notes, including in shared vaults: they are encrypted on your device, and nobody — not your administrators, not Filarr — holds a master key that opens them.
privacy.warning: One exception worth knowing: if your organization set up a recovery key, an encrypted copy of your ORGANIZATION vault keys is entrusted to it, so your access can be returned if you lose your password. This never covers your personal space.

vaults.title: Team vaults
vaults.body: A shared vault behaves like a folder: files, notes, history. The difference is invisible and lies in the key — each member gets their own copy of the vault key, encrypted for them alone. Removing someone from the vault genuinely removes their ability to decrypt it.

settings.title: What your organization can set on your behalf
settings.body: It can impose a session length, require two-factor authentication, restrict external sharing, turn off the marketplace or limit extensions, and apply a theme. When a setting is imposed on you, the app says so where the choice used to be, rather than making it vanish without explanation.

offline.title: Offline
offline.body: The app keeps working without a network under the last rules it received. If your organization set a maximum offline window and it is exceeded, the app locks until the next connection — your data is not lost, only unreachable until then.

leaving.title: If you leave the organization
leaving.body: You lose access to the shared vaults, and your seat frees up for someone else. An organization subscription is not a personal one: it does not follow you, and it is not taken from you either, since it was never yours.

zk.title: What Filarr cannot do
zk.body: We hold no master key. Your files and notes are encrypted on your devices before being sent; we store only unreadable blocks and copies of keys that are themselves encrypted by your passwords. A court order could only compel us to hand that over. This is not a commercial promise we could change our mind about: it is a property of the architecture, and it has a price — if a member loses both their password AND their recovery phrase, only your organization recovery key can still return their organization vaults. Nobody else can, us included.

storage.title: Vault storage
storage.desc: Host the organization’s shared vaults on your own S3-compatible bucket. Content stays end-to-end encrypted: your bucket only ever sees blobs.
storage.upgradeRequired: Organization storage requires a Teams or Enterprise plan.
storage.saved: Storage target saved. Remember to migrate existing vaults.
storage.migrateNeeded: {{count}} object(s) ({{size}}) across {{vaults}} vault(s) still live on Filarr Cloud.
storage.purgeConfirm: Delete the Filarr Cloud copy of the organization’s vaults? The server first verifies every object exists in your bucket.
storage.purgeDiffering: Some objects differ between the two sides (rewritten since the copy). Re-run the migration before purging.
storage.backConfirm: Copy all vaults back to Filarr Cloud first, then remove the organization bucket?

noOrg.title: You do not belong to any organization
noOrg.desc: Your account is indeed an organization account — it is only missing an organization.
noOrg.invited: If your team already uses Filarr, do not create anything: your administrator must send you an email invitation. Its link attaches you to their organization, with the role they chose, and at no cost to you.
noOrg.createDesc: You become its owner. Before you create: a new organization grants nothing until the subscription is taken out — no invitations, no team vaults, no branding. Billing is per seat, minimum three, and viewers are free.

closing.title: {{name}} is being closed
closing.text: Closure has been started. For thirty days everything stays read-only and nothing is destroyed; after that, the organisation, its vaults and its audit log disappear. As an owner you can still cancel it.

publish.title: Publish this vault to your account

intro.heading: This vault already holds your files.
intro.body: This device protects {{items}} items ({{size}}) with its own key. Adopting your account key directly would make them unreadable.
intro.alternative: There is another way: publish this vault to your account. Every item is read, re-encrypted at upload time with the account key, uploaded, verified — and only then does this device change keys.
intro.safety: No file on this device is modified or erased while publishing: you can stop at any moment, losing nothing and with nothing to undo.

inventory.heading: What will be published
inventory.doNotPublishMeaning: A profile you do not publish stays usable on this device, exactly as it is today. It simply will not go to your account, and your other devices will not see it.

verify.body: The account received {{received}} items. We are now re-checking {{sample}} of them by downloading them again, to confirm they read back with the account key.
verify.nothingChanged: Nothing has changed on this device yet.

switch.heading: Last step
switch.body: Everything is verified. This device will now use your account key for everything it writes from here on. Your files on this device and your local password do not change.
switch.retainedKey: This device also keeps its previous key, read-only: that is what lets all your current files keep opening. The trade-off, stated plainly: two vault keys will remain on this device for good.
switch.localOnlyNotice: Profile “{{name}}” ({{count}} items) stays on this device only: it keeps opening here, but it does not exist on your account and your other devices will not see it.

done.heading: Done.
done.body: {{count}} items published. This device now writes with your account key, and keeps its previous key for reading everything that was already there.
done.damaged: {{count}} items could not be read. Their bytes are still on the device; they were already unreadable before.

sharingNudge.title: This account is in use on {{count}} devices
sharingNudge.body: If several of you are working together, a shared vault gives each person their own access: you can see who wrote what, remove someone without changing everyone else’s password, and nobody gets signed out.

compare.title: Sharing an account? There is a better way.
compare.intro: Handing out your password works — until someone leaves, until a note disappears with no way to know who deleted it, or until everything has to change at once.
compare.sharedVaultSub: Everyone has their own account, one vault in common
compare.lost1: Nobody knows who wrote or deleted what.
compare.lost2: Removing someone means changing the password — and signing everyone out.
compare.lost3: Whoever leaves keeps a copy of everything, forever.
compare.lost4: One trash, one history: someone else’s mistake erases your work.
compare.lost5: Three devices at a time, no live typing.
compare.won2: Removing someone takes one click. Nobody else is affected.
compare.won3: Whoever leaves loses access: the vault is resealed.
compare.won4: Read-only, write, administer — case by case.
compare.won5: Live writing together, with no device ceiling.
compare.e2ee: End-to-end encryption does not change: we still cannot read what you write, together or alone.
compare.noPressure: Nothing forces you to change: sharing an account stays possible. This screen exists because most people who do it do not know what it costs them.
